Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 450 AM EST Mon Nov 23 2026
 

- Much colder today and through the rest of the week. 

- Lake effect rain/snow to snow shower potential mainly late this 
  afternoon through this evening. 

- Mostly rain with periods of rain/snow mix for Thursday into Friday.

&&

.AVIATION...

Northwest winds sustained at or above 10 knots, gusting to 20 knots 
at times today, will continue to slowly usher colder and drier air 
into southeast Michigan. Breaks in the clouds have already developed 
over southern Lower Michigan, and a period of ceiling free skies 
appears likely late this morning. An upper level trough/cold pool 
swinging through Lower Michigan early this evening is expected to 
support scattered snow showers or a snow/rain mix late today and 
this evening, mainly north of the southern taf sites. However, the 
inherited prob30 will be maintained for the southern TAFS, while a 
TEMPO MVFR group will be carried for the northern tafs. A dusting of 
snow is possible on the colder and grassy surfaces. Surface winds 
will become northerly in the wake of the upper level trough passage 
tonight, presenting another opportunity to scatter out or clear the 
low clouds. 

For DTW... Variable low VFR clouds today, with a chance of a passing 
snow/rain shower mix between 22-4z Tuesday. Snow is expected to 
mainly melt on contact, as temps likely do not reach freezing until 
midnight.

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* Low in ceilings aob 5000 feet through afternoon, then medium 
  this evening and low overnight.

* Medium confidence in precip type being melting snow this evening.
